author: Yanming Zhu
status: post-result, Introduction-driven exploratory analysis with frozen specifications
conceptual_estimand: a shared neural transformation from sentence-initial NP to post-marker NP across matched Agent and Patient nouns
artifact_policy: apply the threshold only to runs with an available annotation table and require a complete 20-noun matched set after filtering
primary_response: mean 0-800 ms firing rate minus the -500-0 ms baseline, aligned to target-noun onset
outer_cross_validation: leave one complete sentence pair out; train on one thematic-role class and test the other
parallelism_score: cosine between training-set Agent and Patient position-difference vectors after training-only unit standardization
stimulus_null: all 2^10 synchronized within-pair position-label swaps, shared across roles, runs and patients
continuous_time_axis_fit: fit the position axis only from the frozen 0-800 ms training response and project held-out cross-role 5-ms activity

legacy_timepoint_rule.additional_control: patient-level exact max-statistic across the full continuous time grid

scrambled_analysis: train the grammar position axis while leaving out the matched pair, then compare later-minus-earlier noun projection in the five recorded scrambled sentences
anchor_scope: a target-noun position axis is identifiable only at target-noun alignment; marker- and verb-aligned sentence responses are integrated from the separately frozen event-anchor analysis and are not relabelled as noun position observations
multiplicity: report the five prespecified modules jointly; no module is selected for significance
interpretation_limits: surface position is confounded with serial time and preceding marker context
voice is confounded with function-word identity, acoustics and sentence form
Agent and Patient are confounded with animacy and lexical class
cross-role generalization does not identify hierarchical syntax over linear or local-context accounts
scrambled trials are sparse and do not provide an independent confirmatory dataset
